AKOpOmTYO3s.speaker: Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine
AKOpOmTYO3s.summary: Niger's prime minister rejected the narrative of 'a poor Africa' living on aid, and the absence of an African permanent seat. He said 'our Sahel is at war… against a conspiracy aimed at recolonizing it', calling so-called terrorism 'the cynical machinery of recolonization' driven by greed for uranium. He accused France and its proxies of planning attacks on military and oil sites, and called the Alliance of Sahel States 'an irreversible process' toward sovereignty.
AKOpOmTYO3s.primary_concern: A 'war of liberation' against what Niger calls a plot to recolonize the Sahel

mentions.note: accused of destabilizing Sahel, planning attacks

CCxbQdjb_A8.speaker: James Marape
CCxbQdjb_A8.summary: Marape said PNG's 800 languages under one constitution show diversity need not mean division, and that the UN lets the smallest sit with the largest. He urged leaders to weigh future generations in decisions on war, energy, forests, oceans and minerals: 'Put human welfare ahead of war. Put humanity ahead of narrow geopolitical interests.'
CCxbQdjb_A8.primary_concern: Putting human welfare and future generations ahead of war

rm0vxHCCFJo.speaker: Shehbaz Sharif
rm0vxHCCFJo.summary: Sharif said Pakistan faced Indian aggression 'under a false pretext' a year ago and acted in self-defence, and thanked Trump for a 'timely intervention' when two nuclear powers stood at the brink. He said lasting stability needs a just Kashmir settlement and the long-promised plebiscite, and called India's holding the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance illegal, warning that any diversion of Pakistan's water 'will be treated as an act of war'. He touted economic stabilization and CPEC with China.
rm0vxHCCFJo.primary_concern: Kashmir and India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty

ocxTNopUYVE.speaker: Philip J. Pierre
ocxTNopUYVE.summary: Pierre said a loan is not justice when a small nation must borrow to repair damage it did not cause, calling climate finance 'justice, responsibility and survival'. He urged states to meet commitments to Haiti's Gang Suppression Force, reform a Council 'anchored in 1945', and pursue reparatory justice, and warned AI could widen the gap between powerful and vulnerable.
ocxTNopUYVE.primary_concern: Climate finance as justice, not charity

NFtbV2NJT3s.speaker: Matthew Wale
NFtbV2NJT3s.summary: Solomon Islands' prime minister said every fuel price rise hits shipping, electricity and food for islands with no buffer ('there are no winners in war, only graves, orphans'). He sought full capitalization of the Pacific Resilience Facility, a third Green Climate Fund replenishment and ocean finance, noting the world spends in 18 days on arms what rich countries give in a year of climate finance.
NFtbV2NJT3s.primary_concern: Distant wars arriving as fuel and food price shocks

k4A7JfpwgZI.speaker: Hristijan Mickoski
k4A7JfpwgZI.summary: Mickoski said AI, energy and climate will transform societies while over 100 million are displaced: 'technological capability does not automatically produce political wisdom'. He affirmed North Macedonia as a NATO ally with the US as its strategic partner and EU membership its goal, and urged demanding 'relevance, not perfection' from the UN.

vzMvHnQFlwI.speaker: Feleti Teo
vzMvHnQFlwI.summary: Teo said Tuvalu has reclaimed 15.3 hectares of elevated, flood-free land on Funafuti, with 10 more underway, on a nation of 26 km². He highlighted Tuvalu's first police deployment to a UN mission (South Sudan), and urged action on the underfunded ocean goal (SDG 14) for a 'large ocean State'.
vzMvHnQFlwI.primary_concern: Sea-level rise as a present reality

FRqig0GwFT0.speaker: Sam Matekane
FRqig0GwFT0.summary: Matekane credited preventive diplomacy with Lesotho's restored stability, described floods, droughts and land degradation, and sought climate finance and a Just Energy Transition Fund. He noted 38% youth unemployment, defended migrant workers' dignity 'regardless of status', and called for diplomatic solutions in Ukraine, the Middle East, Sudan and eastern DRC.
FRqig0GwFT0.primary_concern: Climate damage and youth unemployment in a least developed country

BeLncM4uDPI.speaker: Robert Abela
BeLncM4uDPI.summary: Abela called lack of trust 'the greatest challenge'. He said peace in Ukraine must guarantee its sovereignty within recognized borders, and that Gaza needs Hamas disarmed and a credible path to a just peace for Palestinians: 'no trust equals no peace'. He called climate change 'the greatest threat to us all' and inaction 'a moral and practical betrayal', against denial-fuelling disinformation.
BeLncM4uDPI.primary_concern: The collapse of trust, and climate change as the greatest threat to islands

d8vsUIpTdcg.speaker: Hilda Heine
d8vsUIpTdcg.summary: Heine demanded a UN apology for the 67 nuclear tests on the Marshall Islands in 1946–58 when it was a UN trust territory: 'the lack of acknowledgment remains a moral failure'. She called continued fossil-fuel investment 'immoral and irrational', said 'it is the seas that are rising, not our islands sinking', sought a seabed-mining moratorium, and urged Taiwan's inclusion in UN meetings.
d8vsUIpTdcg.primary_concern: The UN's unacknowledged role in 67 nuclear tests, and rising seas

rSR4N0q4dw4.speaker: Christophe Mirmand
rSR4N0q4dw4.summary: Monaco's head of government warned that the use of force is becoming ordinary politics and civilians pay the price, quoting Hammarskjöld that the UN exists 'to save humanity from hell'. He hailed the high-seas biodiversity treaty as 'a victory for cooperation over predation', and urged 30% ocean protection by 2030, a plastics treaty and caution on seabed mining.
rSR4N0q4dw4.primary_concern: Force becoming 'an instrument of politics like any other', and protecting the ocean

GtP06obtZaE.speaker: Nawaf Salam
GtP06obtZaE.summary: Salam said weapons must be only in the state's hands and 'no one speaks for Lebanon', which was drawn into 'a war it did not choose'. He sought a permanent ceasefire, Israeli withdrawal to recognized borders, return of detainees and displaced people, and reconstruction via US-mediated talks with Israel. He defended UNRWA and voiced solidarity with Gulf states and Jordan against Iranian attacks.
GtP06obtZaE.primary_concern: Lebanon refusing to be 'a bargaining chip' in others' wars

mentions.note: attacks on Gulf; implicit Hezbollah patron

w-oFlcoDr3E.speaker: Ali Falih Al-Zaidi
w-oFlcoDr3E.summary: Al-Zaidi said the end of the international coalition mission moves Iraq's partnerships from military to economic cooperation, and urged vigilance against extremism. Amid Gulf shipping disruptions, Iraq is diversifying oil export routes through Türkiye, Jordan and Syria, and pitching its Development Road for regional integration: 'Invest in Iraq.' He called a just solution for Palestine central to regional security.
w-oFlcoDr3E.primary_concern: Iraq's Development Road and energy corridors as a path to regional integration

HDVIIPEIKcQ.speaker: Hussain Mohamed Latheef
HDVIIPEIKcQ.summary: Maldives' vice president said sovereignty can be undermined 'without a single border being crossed', and warned big-power rivalry in the Indian Ocean must not limit small states' choices. He condemned Hormuz's closure and attacks on Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Jordan, praised Omani, Pakistani and Qatari mediation, and said 'Israel's genocide and war crimes against Palestinians continue'. He called sea-level rise a matter of national security.
HDVIIPEIKcQ.primary_concern: Climate change and sea-level rise as a matter of sovereignty

mentions.note: implicit: Hormuz closure, attacks on Gulf

J_wnDKwXMKg.speaker: Taneti Maamau
J_wnDKwXMKg.summary: Maamau welcomed the high-seas biodiversity treaty and demanded adequate, predictable adaptation finance as sea-level rise and saltwater intrusion press on Kiribati. He reaffirmed the nuclear-weapons ban treaty and a trust fund for testing victims: 'even the smallest country can contribute to global peace'.
J_wnDKwXMKg.primary_concern: Rising seas threatening a 'Big Ocean' state

gsbO7e9VCfc.summary: Japan answered Russia's statement by stressing eight decades as a 'peace-loving nation' committed to the rule of law and the UN Charter. Guatemala rejected Belize's 'serious accusation' of a military overflight ('this flight never happened'), said it will ask the OAS monitoring mechanism to investigate, and argued the Assembly is not the forum for a dispute before the ICJ.

UeE9RZK7K2o.speaker: Sugiono
UeE9RZK7K2o.summary: Indonesia's foreign minister said 'the answer to imperfect multilateralism is not less multilateralism' and described resilience as families able to provide and children able to learn. He affirmed a diverse Indonesia grounded in democracy and human rights, urged ASEAN to evolve, called Palestine 'a test to our conscience' demanding an end to colonialism, pledged continued commitment to Lebanon as UNIFIL ends, and announced a 2029–30 Council bid.
UeE9RZK7K2o.primary_concern: A multilateralism resilient enough to deliver, and justice for Palestine

F-ZpB9aY_bI.speaker: Mulambo Haimbe
F-ZpB9aY_bI.summary: Zambia's foreign minister said its recent elections proved differences can be managed peacefully and that Zambia is 'open for partnership'. He sought affordable climate finance and adaptation investment ('those who contributed least must not bear the greatest costs'), long-term development finance after Zambia's debt restructuring, and investment in Africa's youth. He backed permanent African Council seats.
F-ZpB9aY_bI.primary_concern: Closing the financing gap for climate-exposed, youthful Africa

ztPI8oFfwnc.speaker: Ilza Amado Vaz
ztPI8oFfwnc.summary: São Tomé and Príncipe's foreign minister said the islands suffer severe climate impacts despite negligible emissions. She wants the vulnerability index turned into concessional-finance eligibility, a working loss-and-damage fund and easier Green Climate Fund access, and pitched the blue economy around its UNESCO biosphere status, with human-centred AI governance.
ztPI8oFfwnc.primary_concern: The 'profound climate injustice' facing a small island state

UiXOnmM3gsg.speaker: Kamina Johnson Smith
UiXOnmM3gsg.summary: Jamaica's foreign minister said Hurricane Melissa (October 2025) caused damage equal to 56.7% of GDP in hours, despite catastrophe insurance and a cat bond that provided liquidity: 'we can do everything right' and still lose decades. She sought accessible climate finance and inclusive AI governance, backed Guyana's Secretary-General candidate, and said gangs 'cannot be allowed to determine Haiti's future'.
UiXOnmM3gsg.primary_concern: Hurricane Melissa's losses of 56.7% of GDP and the limits of preparation

J6a9lGqO4kk.speaker: Anita Anand
J6a9lGqO4kk.summary: Anand said 'great powers are walking away from global economic cooperation' and coercing others 'to accept what we are offered', so Canada is pursuing strategic autonomy: 'we can no longer afford to be overly reliant on any one partner'. She cited 20+ new economic and defence partnerships (Coalition of the Willing, Arctic Seven, Nordic-Baltic Eight), a path to 5% defence spending by 2035, and condemned rising antisemitism after the Belleville synagogue attack, and Islamophobia.
J6a9lGqO4kk.primary_concern: A 'rupture, not a transition' as great powers abandon economic cooperation

yhbILw63f0w.speaker: Marie-Edith Tassyla-Ye-Doumbeneny
yhbILw63f0w.summary: Gabon's foreign minister called for 'substantial strength' to secure the Gulf of Guinea, reform of the financial architecture to fund climate action, and an international legal framework on AI and data privacy (Gabon has passed its own). She called for internal UN reform and Africa's 'rightful place' on the Security Council.
yhbILw63f0w.primary_concern: Security in the Gulf of Guinea and fairer development finance

ZEke1xl5YGw.speaker: Sayyid Badr Albusaidi
ZEke1xl5YGw.summary: Oman's foreign minister said the region saw 'a war that could have been avoided' whose escalation paralysed the Strait of Hormuz, and pledged Oman's continuing effort to safeguard navigation there under UNCLOS, inviting all parties to cooperate. He backed a political solution preserving Yemen's unity, rejected Israel's attacks on Arab states and 'crimes of the Israeli occupation', and promoted the Muscat Plan against hate speech.
ZEke1xl5YGw.primary_concern: 'A war that could have been avoided' and keeping Hormuz open

mentions.note: attacks on Arab states; occupation crimes

UiNwYXcmjb8.speaker: Mohamad Hasan
UiNwYXcmjb8.summary: Malaysia's foreign minister said the UN only counts the dead and rebuilds, and must move to prevention, 'nowhere more urgent than Gaza', which has the most orphans of any single conflict: 'We are sick of it.' He warned a handful of private actors now hold AI power, and insisted 'the Global South cannot simply become a destination for data centres while decisions are made elsewhere'.
UiNwYXcmjb8.primary_concern: Gaza's orphans, and the Global South as more than a market in the AI age

qYTqucfm8Xo.speaker: Abdoulkader Houssein Omar
qYTqucfm8Xo.summary: Djibouti's foreign minister said several thousand people fleeing Yemen have strained its capacity and asked for help, and a peaceful solution in Yemen and free Red Sea navigation. He urged support for Somalia's authorities and de-escalation in Sudan, asking foreign actors to stop fuelling the war.
qYTqucfm8Xo.primary_concern: Yemen's war spilling refugees into Djibouti

VvNTEOD6ziI.speaker: Luca Beccari
VvNTEOD6ziI.summary: San Marino's foreign minister announced its EU Association Agreement signing on 19 October: 'cooperation does not diminish sovereignty'. He backed UN80 and consensus-based Council reform (Uniting for Consensus). He stood by San Marino's recognition of Palestine ('Gaza cannot become the new normal'), and demanded the Taliban reverse restrictions on women and girls.
VvNTEOD6ziI.primary_concern: Small-state sovereignty exercised through cooperation, and a signed EU association

uDX-Gcas9yc.speaker: Mohamed Ali Nafti
uDX-Gcas9yc.summary: Tunisia's foreign minister asked how trust in multilateralism can be restored while Palestinians suffer daily 'horrific crimes', condemning 'genocide' and occupation policies. He urged a migration approach beyond security that tackles root causes, said Tunisia rescues migrants and aids voluntary returns but 'rejects becoming a transit country or destination', and called for equitable AI governance.
uDX-Gcas9yc.primary_concern: A balanced response to migration, and Palestinians denied basic rights

tf_EDmSVVlc.speaker: Sirojiddin Muhriddin
tf_EDmSVVlc.summary: Tajikistan's foreign minister promoted its proposed 2027–36 decade for strengthening peace and a 2028 Dushanbe Water Conference to close the Water Action Decade, stressing glacier loss. He cited its AI-for-development resolution, border agreements with Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan ('borders that once divided us now connect us'), and a first-ever Council bid for 2028–29.
tf_EDmSVVlc.primary_concern: Water and glaciers, and turning borders that divided into borders that connect

Pd9pwQqCQSg.speaker: Johann Wadephul
Pd9pwQqCQSg.summary: Germany's foreign minister noted most AI patents are held by companies in two countries: 'whenever power becomes global, responsibility must become global, too.' He sought common safety requirements for the most capable models ('our institutions have to catch up with reality'), and a next Secretary-General who leads deep reform. He urged pressure on Russia to negotiate ('the future is built at the negotiating table, not on dead bodies'), and rejected nationalism and raw materials as leverage.
Pd9pwQqCQSg.primary_concern: Concentrated power over AI, which two countries dominate

mentions.note: implicit: AI concentration; raw materials as pressure

CuSDv4Ftiow.speaker: Subrahmanyam Jaishankar
CuSDv4Ftiow.summary: Jaishankar said wars now penalize countries far from them through food, energy and trade disruptions, and 'those most impacted often have the least say'. He called for de-escalation in the Gulf and protection of shipping and seafarers, peace in Ukraine ('endless war must give way to an end to war'), and two states for Palestine. He warned of a 'weaponization of everything' from finance to supply chains, and of persistent terrorism, with a pointed warning to Pakistan that friendship cannot coexist with it. He defended each nation's right to build its own AI models.
CuSDv4Ftiow.primary_concern: Distant wars and the 'weaponization of everything' punishing bystanders

yzBZyEw5LMY.speaker: Ludwing Jaentschke Whitaker
yzBZyEw5LMY.summary: Nicaragua's foreign minister called drug trafficking and organized crime forms of terrorism and praised BRICS. He voiced solidarity with Cuba, backed the 'non-negotiable' One-China principle, and said Nicaragua shares 'the struggle against fascism and the right to peace waged by the Russian Federation'.
yzBZyEw5LMY.primary_concern: Poverty and the fight against 'fascism', alongside Russia and BRICS

CxIZRezqyG0.speaker: Vivian Balakrishnan
CxIZRezqyG0.summary: Balakrishnan said interstate relations dictated by raw power are 'a clear and present danger' for small states, and pointed to WFP, ICAO and ITU as proof multilateralism works. He said the Gulf war has put UNCLOS under 'a severe stress test', while three littoral states keep the Strait of Singapore open for a quarter of seaborne trade. He called AI 'the most urgent frontier', insisting humans 'remain in control and accountable'.
CxIZRezqyG0.primary_concern: Raw power endangering small states, and AI as 'the most urgent frontier'

iUXOE4G07BU.speaker: Thorgerdur Katrín Gunnarsdóttir
iUXOE4G07BU.summary: Iceland's foreign minister said the world's best moments, from the Human Rights Council to the ICC and UNFCCC, came when leaders chose cooperation. The next Secretary-General must keep reforming — 'Yes, her.' 'We choose international law over selective obedience. Accountability over impunity.'
iUXOE4G07BU.primary_concern: Choosing cooperation over retreat, as the UN's founders did

C63mBZXfNns.speaker: Prince Faisal bin Farhan
C63mBZXfNns.summary: Prince Faisal said Saudi Arabia and its neighbours suffered 'flagrant Iranian attacks' and reaffirmed the right to self-defence. He demanded Hormuz return to its pre-28 February status with no fees or restrictions, rejected waterways as tools of pressure, and sought a region free of weapons of mass destruction. He condemned Houthi attacks, backed Syria's territorial integrity, warned Iraq's territory must not be a launchpad, and highlighted Saudi AI capacity-building centres.
C63mBZXfNns.primary_concern: 'Flagrant Iranian attacks' and restoring Hormuz to its pre-28 February status

mentions.note: must not be launchpad for attacks

MTtO-YXn0Co.speaker: Sergey Lavrov
MTtO-YXn0Co.summary: Lavrov said the Global South and East are rising as sovereign centres while 'the Western minority' tries to keep its privileges. He deplored the US invasion of Venezuela and demanded Maduro's release, and called the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei 'coercive dictate'. He backed Palestinian statehood, accused the EU of forcing Serbia to accept Kosovo's loss and of torpedoing Trump-era peace talks, and said the US created a 'Russophobic regime in Kyiv'. He vowed the 'special military operation' objectives will be achieved, backed Brazil and India for permanent seats, and opposed seats for Germany and Japan.
MTtO-YXn0Co.primary_concern: A 'Western minority' clinging to 500 years of privilege against a rising Global South and East

mentions.note: invasion of Venezuela; destroyed European security (though credits interest in peace)

utivTYXBmoA.speaker: Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla
utivTYXBmoA.summary: Rodríguez said Washington's bid 'to impose peace through force' is unrealizable, listing 'the genocidal crime of Zionism', killings in the Caribbean, aggression against Venezuela and the war on Iran. He said the US fuel blockade since January 2026 is an act of war and 'collective punishment', blocking aid and scaring off investors, in the tradition of the 1960 Mallory memo: 'Cuba is not a threat. The blockade is.' 'The law of the jungle cannot be the future of humanity.'
utivTYXBmoA.primary_concern: US 'multidimensional aggression', including a fuel blockade he calls an act of war

mentions.note: blockade as act of war; aggression

sd08XAWI1lU.speaker: Theresa Lazaro
sd08XAWI1lU.summary: The Philippines' foreign secretary said over 25% of the world's seafarers are Filipino, and two were recently killed in the Strait of Hormuz: 'maritime security is human security'. She called UNCLOS 'the constitution of the oceans', marked ten years of the binding 2016 South China Sea arbitral award ('diplomacy and law, not violence and might'), and proposed an UNCLOS-based framework for protecting critical undersea infrastructure.
sd08XAWI1lU.primary_concern: Seafarers' safety and maritime security, from Hormuz to the South China Sea

GxzETAmL1sw.speaker: Thongsavanh Phomvihane
GxzETAmL1sw.summary: Lao PDR's deputy prime minister called Palestine 'an enduring test of multilateral credibility' and backed an independent Palestinian state. He urged lifting coercive measures on Cuba and removing it from the terror list, and called for climate finance matching ambition. He said clearing five decades of unexploded ordnance is 'not merely a technical task' but about reclaiming land and development.
GxzETAmL1sw.primary_concern: Unexploded wartime ordnance still blocking development

GkZFomdIKD8.speaker: Cardinal Pietro Parolin
GkZFomdIKD8.summary: Cardinal Parolin, citing Pope Leo, warned against a 'diplomacy of force' and called disarmament 'a necessary vehicle'. He said the passing of time does not make Ukraine's war 'any less intolerable' and backed an immediate ceasefire, urged an end to violence against Palestinians in the West Bank and a two-state path, voiced concern over hunger and displacement from the Gulf war, and said the Rohingya's suffering 'must end'.
GkZFomdIKD8.primary_concern: A return to the 'diplomacy of force'

rsVMOdEHpDk.speaker: Vasile Tofan
rsVMOdEHpDk.summary: Tofan said Moldova has 'decided' between East and West. He recalled Soviet deportations and Moscow's use of gas and trade as leverage, and said Moldovans rejected Kremlin disinformation, cyberattacks and vote-buying ('their home is not for sale'). He called Russian troops in Transnistria illegal and demanded their withdrawal, said 'nations are not bargaining chips', offered Moldova as an AI regulatory sandbox, and announced a bid to preside over the 82nd General Assembly.
rsVMOdEHpDk.primary_concern: Russian pressure and troops in Transnistria, and anchoring Moldova in Europe

musW-fEJUEw.speaker: Aren Palik
musW-fEJUEw.summary: Micronesia's vice president said security is shaped by climate fragility as well as conflict. He backed a Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty, highlighted rising marine- and vector-borne illness, and urged stronger ocean governance, fisheries management and action on plastic pollution.

Lnw1sY5eLiE.speaker: Han Zheng
Lnw1sY5eLiE.summary: Vice President Han Zheng said 'the world wants peace, not war', rejecting a 'cold-war mindset and bloc confrontation', and promoted China's four global initiatives. He said major countries should lead in obeying rules. He backed 'Palestinians governing Palestine' in the West Bank and Gaza, said China will play a constructive role 'in its own way' on Ukraine, and demanded an immediate end to the Cuba blockade. He put development at the centre, said 'protectionism produces no winners' against decoupling, and argued AI must be 'for good' and close the digital divide.
Lnw1sY5eLiE.primary_concern: Defending the UN-centred order against bloc confrontation, and development for the Global South
